result.title: To Align or Not To Align: Check Your COMPASS Before You Train
result.summary: Combining pretrained models is a common strategy for building AI systems, whether by aligning a vision encoder with a language model or merging fine-tuned checkpoints. However, finding compatible pairs typically requires costly empirical search, as compatibility is known only after alignment or merging. We propose COMPASS (COMPatibility ASsessment Score), a theoretically motivated diagnostic that estimates whether a model pair will be compatible prior to alignment or merging. Building on the observation that representational convergence is most robust at the level of local neighborhoods, COMPASS decomposes model compatibility into two cheap-to-compute axes: a pair-specific ease, defined as the $k$-NN overlap between the two encoders, and a paradigm-level ceiling, capturing the maximum overlap their training paradigms allow. Together, these two axes provide a ranking of candidate model pairs and prescribe how to act on each pair: (i) prioritize pairs that already agree and whose paradigms are compatible, (ii) invest additional compute on pairs with compatible paradigms but low initial agreement, (iii) switch the pretraining paradigm when it cannot support sufficient agreement, or (iv) deprioritize pairs that score poorly on both axes. We apply COMPASS to $72$ cross-modal alignment experiments and $392$ task-arithmetic model merges and show that compatibility estimates by COMPASS strongly correlate with downstream success, achieving average Pearson correlation of $0.91$ on cross-modal alignment tasks and $0.70$ on model merging.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 COMPASS，一种在跨模态对齐或模型合并之前估计模型对兼容性的诊断指标：用两个编码器间的 k-NN 重叠刻画「配对的易对齐程度」，并用训练范式允许的最大重叠刻画「范式上限」，据此对候选模型对排序并给出是否追加算力的建议，在 72 组跨模态对齐与 392 次模型合并实验中显示与下游成功度的强相关。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「局部邻域重叠衡量表示收敛」的思路，可能可借用作廉价诊断，检查视觉编码器特征是否保留局部结构、进而判断 latent 状态中视觉证据是否坍缩或走视觉旁路；但该工作面向训练期对齐/合并的配对选择，与推理期 latent 生成与使用仍有距离，可供核查。
